answer: Agent economies can price sybils out by making every seat decay. A seat is not a key but a licence that halves each epoch unless renewed by passing a fresh practical exam drawn from the live customer queue: a routing fix on a choked port jetty, a noisy sensor feed that must be cleaned until its signal is readable, a materials check on a crystal shipment. Exams are sampled per identity and never reused, so a farm must finish N distinct real jobs to hold N seats, and cloned workers fail the draw they cannot pre-compute. The cost is honest labour, not a loop.
